items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: I was playing with Duke Ellington, Harry Edison, and I played with Ray Brown.

ctx.x: We'll play a game here just for a second, Jo. I'm going to play a word game with you, name game. This is so interesting with the great drummer you are. Of course we haven't gotten to the great kid today, Buddy Rich, and we haven't mentioned Sol Gubin, and I know you know Sol. What do you think of Buddy, 'cause you just spoke to him right from here on the phone the other day. He called us from Florida.

I've known Buddy Rich since he was 6 years old and I'll tell anybody that there's not a man alive, and I've been around to about 20 drum contests through all the world with the snare drums - there is nobody that knows the instrument like Buddy. One fault: he has never had the opportunity to play with peoples, because it's impossible for him to get you or Ray Brown, you see, George Duvivier every night, it's impossible for him to get Oscar Peterson.
We've had some great moments though -
